beginner.confidence: Low–moderate, and lower than a same-morning report. Weather is turning drier with trades returning and the NWS Honolulu zone page shows no active hazards, but Saturday morning is still only about 40 hours after Thursday's island-wide Flash Flood Warning ended (inside DOH's ~48-hour flushing guidance), the live DOH advisory list could not be read, and a new long-period south swell (model 17–20 s forerunners) is due Saturday afternoon. The morning on-site check decides.
beginner.headline: Tomorrow (Sat Oct 10): conditional for beginners. Trades return (ENE about 10–15 mph, gusts near 18–19 mph in models), drier weather, and water should be clearing, but it is still inside the 48-hour runoff flush after Thursday's flash flooding, so water color decides. Exposed south shores 5–7 ft (NWS), Canoes far smaller; a new long-period south swell starts showing in the afternoon. Evening forecast: confidence is lower than a morning report, and the morning on-site check decides.
beginner.recommendation: Plan tentatively for 10:30 AM–1:30 PM: tide rising off the 10:07 AM low, the lightest wind of the day in model runs (about 8–9 mph), and the most flushing time before the wind builds and the new long-period swell's forerunners arrive mid-afternoon. Go only if the water at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains / Ala Wai side is visibly clear and several full set cycles look manageable. One student or a small group of strong adults; multiple students or children only with clear water and low drift. Trades at Waikīkī blow cross-offshore, so watch for seaward drift of students and boards. After about 1:30 PM expect stronger wind and longer-period, more surging sets.

general.headline: Moderate long-period south swell eases slightly Saturday (NWS 5–7 ft exposed south shores) before a new long-period reinforcement builds late Saturday, peaking Sunday–Monday just below advisory.
